questions.q: What is the cost of a slow or unavailable desktop for your users each day?
questions.need: The cost of poor desktop experience is known
questions.how: Agree a figure with the business, per user per hour
questions.listen: Minutes lost per user per day, times the users, is the figure.
questions.probe: Which team complains most, and what does it cost them?

questions.q: Which users must work from anywhere, and on which devices?
questions.need: The user groups, their locations and their devices are known
questions.how: List the user groups with their needs
questions.listen: Contractors, call centres and remote staff often justify virtual desktops on their own.
questions.probe: How are contractors given access today, and how long does it take?

questions.q: How many desktop pools exist, and who manages each?
questions.why: Pools run apart are updated apart.
questions.need: Every desktop pool is known and managed in one place
questions.how: Register every pool with the console
questions.listen: Many small pools managed differently multiply the work.
questions.probe: Which brokering software runs them, and when does its contract end?

questions.q: How many golden images are there, and how old are they?
questions.why: Image sprawl is the main operational cost.
questions.need: Images are few, current and owned
questions.how: Consolidate images and set an update cadence
questions.listen: Many old images mean patching takes days.
questions.probe: How long does it take to roll a new image out to everyone?

questions.q: How long does a logon take on a Monday morning?
questions.why: Logon time is what users feel first.
questions.need: Logon time meets the agreed target
questions.how: Measure logon times and fix the slowest step
questions.listen: Slow logons at peak point to storage or profiles: measure them in the proof.
questions.probe: What is the logon time target, and who measures it?

questions.q: Can a user reach their desktop from a personal device without leaving data on it?
questions.why: Secure access without data on the device is the point.
questions.need: Remote access is secured and leaves no data on devices
questions.how: Put a gateway with strong sign-in in front of every pool
questions.listen: Access from personal devices with nothing left behind is a common driver.
questions.probe: Which users already work from personal devices?

questions.q: What happens when demand peaks or a site fails?
questions.why: Capacity for peaks and failures decides the design.
questions.need: Peaks and site failures are absorbed without users noticing
questions.how: Plan burst capacity and test it once
questions.listen: Without a second site or room to grow, one failure stops everyone.
questions.probe: Has a site failure ever stopped the desktops, and for how long?

questions.q: Who looks at experience data and decides what to fix?
questions.why: Monitoring without an owner changes nothing.
questions.need: A named owner reviews experience data and acts on it
questions.how: Name the owner and agree a monthly review
questions.listen: Without experience data, fixes follow the loudest complaint.
questions.probe: Which tool measures the users' experience today?

questions.q: How many users are there in all, and how many connect at the same time at peak?
questions.why: Concurrent users size the platform; named users size licences and profile storage.
questions.need: Named users and peak concurrent users are known
questions.how: Take the broker's peak concurrency over a month
questions.listen: Shift work can mean many named users for few desktops: size each separately.
questions.probe: When is the peak, and does it move with shifts or time zones?

questions.q: Which groups need which desktops: task workers, knowledge workers, power users, graphics users?
questions.why: Each group has a profile that sets how many desktops fit on a server.
questions.need: User groups and their profiles are defined
questions.how: Group users by the applications and resources they use
questions.listen: Graphics or engineering users need GPUs and a test of their own.
questions.probe: Which applications need a graphics card, and how many monitors, at what resolution?

questions.q: Do users need desktops that keep their changes, or fresh ones from a shared image, and why?
questions.why: The choice changes storage, density and day-to-day operations.
questions.need: Persistent and fresh desktops are decided per group
questions.how: Agree for each group whether its desktops keep changes
questions.listen: Desktops that keep everything are a common default and a costly one: ask who truly needs it.
questions.probe: Which users install their own software, and why?

questions.q: Where do user profiles and data live, and how large are they per user?
questions.why: Profiles and home drives drive logon time and storage.
questions.need: Where profiles and user data live, and their size, is known
questions.how: Measure the average profile and home drive size
questions.listen: Large profiles loaded at logon slow the mornings; keeping data apart from the profile helps.
questions.probe: How long does logon take for the user with the largest profile?

questions.q: Which security agents run inside the desktops, and how much do they slow them?
questions.why: Agents inside every desktop can cut density sharply.
questions.need: Security agents and their overhead are known
questions.how: List the agents in the golden image and test their load
questions.listen: Scans running on every desktop at once can freeze a cluster: ask how they are scheduled.
questions.probe: When do full scans run, and on how many desktops at once?

questions.q: What does a desktop cost per user per month today, counting licences, hardware, support and the help desk?
questions.why: The cost per user is what any new design is compared with.
questions.need: The cost per user of today's desktops is known, and agreed with finance
questions.how: Add up licences, hardware, data centre, support and help desk calls, and divide by users
questions.listen: A figure per user that finance recognises; "it is in the IT budget" means the comparison will be argued later.
questions.probe: Which part of that cost would finance most like to see go down?
